walkthroughs.body_html:
Biodiversity & Conservation — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Biodiversity & Conservation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Biodiversity & Conservation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: MacArthur and Wilson published island biogeography theory in:
IUCN Red List category 'EN' stands for:
options: Endemic
Endangered
Environmental
Extinct in nature

mcqs.q: Why are top predators most affected by persistent pollutants like mercury?
options: Biomagnification concentrates pollutants at each trophic level up the food chain.
Predators are exposed to more pollution directly.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Predators have weaker immune systems.

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.
Because plants only use carbon.
Industrial chemicals being dumped.
Dissolved CO2 forms carbonic acid, lowering ocean pH.
Predators have weaker immune systems.
Acid rain falling on the ocean.
